doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: Playing at the Budweiser, 1935-42
summary: Rene plays five years at the Budweiser with Rapp, Young, Handy and Decou after the owner hires the Rena brothers. The band ends in 1942 amid killings, his religion and a hard-drinking bandmate.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. Let's see. No, that's when I'm 32. And then 35 I went out there. You know where we talk about the Budweiser?

I know where you, on Ivyville. Yeah, that's right. I played there five years. I played from, oh, I retired. I played from 35 up to 42. 35 up to 42 I played there with a fella that's called Rap. I don't know if you've already talked about him. Played guitar. Rap, yeah, that's right. And young, you call him Spook. And handy, played the bass. And Decaugé, you might have heard him talk about him. I would have been playing the write-up about him. Decaugé. No, I don't think I know.
No? That was a wonderful piano player.

Yeah. Decaugé, yeah. And did you have on there? Yeah. Eh? Decaugé, uh, well, we had, uh, when I went, they had, they got rid of this band. See, because a couple of the musicians quit the thing, and they got rid of them. So, the man told them, say, I know two fellas out in Gitts, I'm gonna see them. He said, that's, uh, Rainey, Kid Rainey and his brother, Joe Rainey. So they came and got us, man. We went up in there, man. Kept that house packed. We kept that house packed for them number of years. Then in 42, well, because they got killed. I mean, right above, they got killed. Stabbed. Well, them fellas, well, them fellas, uh, they didn't like the religion I had. They didn't like the religion. So, they said, if I catch you asleep, we're gonna find him. And so what they did, they got rid of me, see, because I would, you know, drink a long water, you see. This fella spoke young, I don't know if you know. Boy, that fella used to get drunk every night. Then he'd get off and go at the light and you could, around 10 o'clock, 11 o'clock in the daytime, you could find him around Ramport Street Stagg. And I don't understand. And he was a great musician. Anything you throw up there, he could play it right off just like that.
